research.website_note: The results describe Linear, the product development tool at linear.app.

strategy.observation: Linear serves a very large base of product teams and positions itself as the system those teams use for product development, across issue tracking/project management and newer human-plus-agent workflows.
strategy.offer_link: A service that recruits and schedules customer interview participants could help Linear’s product organization run more user research with its own product-team audience, especially if they want to validate workflows like PRDs, issue tracking, and agent-assisted collaboration without spending time on logistics.
hypotheses: Linear’s product team may regularly conduct customer interviews as part of product discovery and roadmap validation.
They may want a faster way to source participants from a large customer base of product teams.
The Head of Product may care about reducing the operational overhead of scheduling interviews across multiple stakeholders and time zones.
strategy.angle: Linear already serves 40,000+ product teams, so I wondered if your team is still handling customer interview recruiting and scheduling manually.
strategy.fit_reason: The fit is plausible because Linear is itself a product-team platform with a large user base, so a participant recruiting/scheduling service could support its own product research. The connection is indirect, though, since the facts don’t confirm an active research-ops bottleneck.

draft.subject: Customer interview logistics
draft.body:
Linear already serves 40,000+ product teams, so I wondered if customer interview recruiting and scheduling is still manual on your side.

Linear is built for issue tracking, PRDs, and shared human-plus-agent workflows. If your product team is validating those areas with customers, I can recruit participants and schedule the sessions.

That would keep the logistics off your team.

Would you want help with recruiting and scheduling customer interviews?

draft.subject: Customer interviews at scale
draft.body:
Linear already serves 40,000+ product teams, so I wondered if your team is still handling customer interview recruiting and scheduling manually.

You work across issue tracking, PRDs, and human-plus-agent workflows. If product research is part of how you validate those areas, I could help by recruiting participants and lining up sessions for your team.

The goal would be simple: less logistics, more time with users.

Would it be worth a brief look?

issues: The line “You work across issue tracking, PRDs, and human-plus-agent workflows” attributes those workflows to the recipient. Change it to a company fact, e.g. “Linear supports issue tracking, PRDs, and human-plus-agent workflows.”
“The goal would be simple: less logistics, more time with users.” reads like a slogan. Replace it with plain language that states the offer directly.
“Would it be worth a brief look?” is vague and salesy. End with one specific question about whether they want help with recruiting and scheduling customer interviews.
